documents.unit: Office of the Provost and Division of Student Affairs
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy Reminder (letter to students)
documents.quality_note: Short provost/dean letter, but it is CMU's authoritative statement: generative AI counts as 'unauthorized assistance' unless the instructor explicitly permits it. Only a few AI sentences; 2023 and not reissued.

documents.unit: Eberly Center for Teaching Excellence and Educational Innovation
documents.title: Examples of possible academic integrity policies that address student use of generative AI tools
documents.quality_note: Eberly Center page that restates the university position and gives sample syllabus statements ranging from prohibition to permitted-with-citation. Advisory examples, not binding rules.

notes: The CMU University Policy on Academic Integrity (cmu.edu/policies/student-and-student-life/academic-integrity.html, last administrative update Aug 15, 2024) was fetched and contains no AI text, so it was not collected; the provost letter says it covers generative AI via 'unauthorized assistance'. Not collected: Computing Services Generative AI hub and 'Use AI Safely at CMU' (tool and data-safety pages; hub page fetched is navigation only), Career & Professional Development Center AI guidance for students (job-search advice), Eberly AI tools hub. Computing: searched School of Computer Science and department sites (cs.cmu.edu, csd.cmu.edu, ml.cmu.edu); found only course syllabi (known URLs 10-301/601, 10-315, 15-112, 15-122, 95-865 are all course layer, deferred) and search hits for program handbooks (not opened). No SCS-wide or department-level AI policy found. LTI/MSAII master's handbooks (AY2025-26, 2026-27) exist and were not opened; they could be checked later for AI language.
